Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

At 1.30 p.m. on 27-3-38 the informant Zah Kwoh
Tsung, a coolie employed by the "Li Pao" Newspaper
Office, 289 Kiukiang Road, came to the Station and
reported that a burnt out bomb had been found in lane
286 Shantung Road.

C.D.C.44 and the undersigned accompanied by F.S.
Luffy and party immediately attended and learnt the
following:-

At 1.20 p.m. on 27-3-38 an old woman named Siaq
Daung Sz 〔此处转录不清〕 , whose husband is employed as a
coolie was in Lane 286 Shantung Road and heard a
peculiar "sizzling" noise which appeared to emanate
from behind a large roll of white paper standing
immediately outside the rear entrance to the newspaper
offices. She investigated and found an object which
looked like a large tin, right in the corner behind
the paper, which was burning and bubbling over. She
picked it up and on noticing a liquid oozing out threw
it onto the ground whereupon a very slight explosion
was heard and it caught alight for a moment, then
burnt out.

The remnants of this bomb was brought to the
Station where it was found to consist of a "Thermos"
type flask containing three dry batteries bound
together, a small round piece of clockwork mechanism
with two hands and a small metal container which when
examined was empty. All these objects were connected
by wires. The lid or cup of the flask was quite
intact but the flask itself was broken down one side

备注
（任何突出或特殊的特征需由调查警官评论）。

1938年3月27日下午1:30，报案人张国宗（Zah Kwoh Tsung，音译），系九江路289号《立报》馆雇佣的苦力，来到捕房报告称在山东路286弄发现一枚烧毁的炸弹。

刑事侦缉处长44号（C.D.C.44）及本人，在法医助理拉菲（F.S. Luffy）及其随行人员陪同下立即前往现场，获悉以下情况：—

1938年3月27日下午1:20，一位名叫夏当氏（Siaq Daung Sz，此处转录不清）的老妇人在山东路286弄，其丈夫受雇为苦力。她听到一种奇特的“嘶嘶”声，似乎发自报社后门外立着的一卷大白纸后面。她上前查看，发现在纸张后面的角落里有一个看起来像大锡罐的物体，正在燃烧并冒泡。她将其捡起，注意到有液体渗出，便将其扔在地上，随即听到一声非常轻微的爆炸声，物体短暂起火，随后熄灭。

这枚炸弹的残骸被带到捕房，经检查发现由一个“保温瓶”式样的热水瓶组成，内含三节捆扎在一起的干电池、一个带有两根指针的小型圆形钟表机械装置，以及一个小型金属容器，经查为空。所有这些物体均由电线连接。热水瓶的盖子或杯盖完好无损，但瓶身一侧破裂

pointing to some sort of explosion, however small, having occurred. From this it would appear to be some sort of homemade time bomb which through poor workmanship failed to go off but burnt itself out. Possibly intended to be of any incendiary nature.

D.S.I. Mason of the F.P. Bureau was telephoned and came to the Station where he took photos of the bomb.

Since Nov. 25th 1937 the "Li Pao" Newspaper has not been published but the printing machinery and staff are hired by the "Dah Mei Wan Pao", 19 Avenue Edward VII, to print copies of the evening edition due to the increased circulation of the latter newspaper.

It is mentioned that these particular premises were bombed on a previous occasion, i.e. 4-3-38, when an unknown male Chinese threw a "potato masher" type grenade at the front door. (Please see Central F.I.R. Cll/38) Prior to that bombing, Mr. Samuel Chang, the proof reader for the "Dah Mei Wan Pao" received several threatening letters but since that occurrence no more have been received by any of the staff, and nothing untoward has happened.

Enquiries at the offices learnt that the large roll of paper behind which the bomb was hidden was placed there at about 3 p.m. on 26-3-38 and was not touched until the bomb was discovered. This bomb, therefore, could have been

表明曾发生过某种程度的爆炸，无论多么微小。由此看来，这似乎是一种自制定时炸弹，因制作工艺拙劣未能引爆而自行烧毁。可能意在纵火。

已电话通知法证局（F.P. Bureau）的梅森副督察（D.S.I. Mason），他来到捕房对炸弹进行了拍照。

自1937年11月25日起，《立报》已停止出版，但其印刷设备和人员被爱多亚路19号的《大美晚报》租用，以印刷该报因发行量增加而需要的晚刊。

据悉，该处所此前曾遭轰炸，即1938年3月4日，一名身份不明的中国男子向前门投掷了一枚“土豆捣碎器”式手榴弹。（请参阅中央火灾/事故报告 Cll/38）在那次轰炸之前，《大美晚报》的校对员塞缪尔·张（Samuel Chang）先生收到过几封恐吓信，但自那以后，任何职员均未再收到此类信件，也未发生其他异常事件。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
placed there at any time between 3 p.m. 26-3-38 and the
time of discovery. The lane is very populous, many people
hawkers, coolies employed at the newspaper offices, etc.
always being present. All those available of the staff,
including Mr. D.F. Dien(田丹伟), were questioned but no
one was found who could shed any light on the affair. A
private watchman, Lung Kyi Zung(陳继仁) by name is employ-
ed by the "Li Pao" newspaper office, to look after the
lane as people are always working therein, but when
questioned he stated that he noticed no suspicious person
entering and in any case remarked that he would probably
not stop anyone carrying what looked like a vacuum flask.
Since the previous bombing on 4-3-38 a C.P.C. has
been placed outside the front entrance to the offices
day and night, and at the time of the present case, C.P.C.
1842 was on duty. The rear entrance to the office is,
however, about 80 yards down a winding lane which in turn
is about 100 yards from the front entrance on Kiukiang
Road, so no information could be gained from him.
From the foregoing, although the bomb was found out-
side the premises of the "Li Pao", it is thought from
past happenings that an attack was directed at the "Dah
Mei Wan Pao" as the premises were being used by them. This
attack is probably connected with the previous bombing
and is a further example of activity directed against the
newspaper.

调查记录。
在1938年3月26日下午3点至发现时间之间的任何时段放置于此。该弄堂人口稠密，许多小贩、报社雇佣的苦力等经常在此。对所有在场的职员，包括田丹伟（Mr. D.F. Dien）先生，进行了询问，但未发现任何人能提供有关此案的线索。《立报》馆雇佣了一名名为陈继仁（Lung Kyi Zung）的私人更夫看守弄堂，因为人们常在其中工作，但经询问，他表示未注意有可疑人员进入，并且无论如何他指出，他大概不会拦阻携带看似真空保温瓶的人。
自1938年3月4日上次轰炸以来，办公室正门前日夜均有中国巡捕（C.P.C.）站岗，本案发生时，由1842号中国巡捕值班。然而，办公室的后门位于一条蜿蜒的弄堂深处约80码处，而该弄堂距离九江路的前门约100码，因此无法从他那里获得任何信息。
综上所述，虽然炸弹是在《立报》馆址外发现的，但根据以往事件判断，袭击目标是《大美晚报》，因为该处所正由其使用。此次袭击可能与之前的轰炸有关，是针对该报活动的又一例证。

was received at this Station from a man named Yang
Yoong Soong (楊耀松), clerk, employee of a Chinese

On receipt of the said telephone message Chief
Inspector Bishop and party of Police immediately
proceeded to the scene of the crime.

From enquiries made by C.I.S.1.9, C.D.C.261 and
the undersigned, the following particulars of this
case had been ascertained.

At about 6.30 p.m. on March 4th an unknown male
Chinese as described on the 1st page of this diary,
approached the office of a Chinese newspaper "Lee
Pao" situated at 289 Kiukiang Road and threw a hand-
grenade of "potato masher" type at the front door of
the office. The front door was locked from inside
and protected by an iron grille from outside.

The hand-grenade struck the iron grille and
fell on the footpath in front of the door and
exploded. The glass of the door and the window had
been smashed by the explosion.

The fragments of the hand-grenade travelled
across the road and three persons who had been work-
ing at the time in the Sai Ziang Kyi Painting Shop,
situated opposite the offices of "Lee Pao" at No.
290 Kiukiang Road, had been injured by the said
fragments: |

From enquiries made it appears that the "Lee Pao" is owned by 8 Chinese partners and managed by a man named Nyi Ngau Sun(戴浮声), who is at present in Hongkong.

The owners suspended publication of the newspaper on November 25th 1937 on orders received from the Special Branch, S.M.P., since that time the newspaper was not published. A Chinese newspaper "Lan Mei Wan Pao" published by the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury is printed at present at the printing department of the "Lee Pao".

It appears that owing to increased circulation of the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury there was not enough machinery to print the "Lan Mei Wan Pao" at 19 Avenue Edward VII. Mr. Starr of the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury through a man named Lee Tsing Ying(李俊英), approached the managers of the "Lee Pao" in December 1937 and arranged printing of the Evening edition of the "Lan Mei Wan Pao" by the former printers of the "Lee Pao" on payment of $2,000.00 per month. Mr. Starr is at present absent from Shanghai but Mr. George Bruce, publisher of the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, visited the station at the request of the undersigned. | |

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Mr. G. Bruce stated that the morning edition of the "Dah Mei Wan Pao" is published by the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury for the last six years and the newspaper is registered in the French Consulate.

Owing to the increased circulation of the said newspaper the publisher decided to issue an evening edition of the same newspaper. As there was not enough machinery to print the newspaper at the printing department of the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, 19 Avenue Edward VII, the management of the "Lee Pao" had been approached, and they agreed to print the "Dah Mei Wan Pao" morning and evening editions(Morning 45,000 copies and Evening 42,000 copies).

It appears that all articles which appear in the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury are usually translated in Chinese and then inserted in the "Dah Mei Wan Pao". Mr. Samuel Chang, employee of the newspaper, usually reads the translations before the same are published in the newspaper. This fact evidently became known to the members of the terrorist gang and they sent him 3 threatening letters.

The last letter was received in the end of February 1938. The letters were sent to 19 Avenue Edward VII, F.C.

It appears that Mr. G. Bruce was approached by the Japanese Censors with the request to send the proofs of

Mau Zien Tai (毛全泰) Furniture Shop before 1935. In

Lien-ching established the Tai Shan (泰山) Furniture
Shop, which, however, subsequently closed down owing to lack
of business. In 1936, Mau contracted to furnish the
"Paradise Dancing Hall." Later he attempted to take over
the management of the ball room, but did not succeed owing
to lack of support from the shareholders. At present, he
lives a quiet life with his family at 83, Sun Avenue. His
name does not appear on the records of this Branch.

Avenue, that is, 81 Sun Avenue, is occupied by the Women's

formerly located at 169 Yuen Ming Yuen Road and removed to

Japanese Hostilities in Shanghai. According to the
records of this Branch, this association has been engaged
on a moderate scale in political activities in Shanghai,
especially in connection with the woman suffrage movement
in 1935 when it demanded equality with men, at the 5th
National Congress. The chairman is Miss Wong Lih-ming
(王立明), wife of Dr. Herman C.E. Liu, President of the

由 刑事侦缉员 施子良（Sih Tse-liang，音译）制作 经由 克劳福德（C. Crawford）侦探长转呈。

关于特务科副侦探长就所附报告所作的批示，谨陈述如下：毛连卿（Mau Lien-ching），系2月15日晚8时15分发生“马铃薯捣碎器”式手榴弹爆炸案的孙科路83号房屋的主要承租人，在1935年之前是“毛全泰”（Mau Zien Tai）家具店的店主。那一年，该店出售给其他利益方，毛连卿创办了“泰山”（Tai Shan）家具店，但该店后因生意清淡而关闭。1936年，毛氏承包了“天堂舞厅”（Paradise Dancing Hall）的家具供应业务。后来他试图接管该舞厅的经营管理，但因缺乏股东支持而未成功。目前，他与家人在孙科路83号过着平静的生活。他的名字未出现在本科的记录中。

值得注意的是，孙科路83号的隔壁，即孙科路81号，由中国妇女禁酒协会（Women's Temperance Association of China）占用。该协会原址位于圆明园路169号，在上海中日敌对行动爆发后迁至现址。根据本科记录，该协会在上海从事适度规模的政治活动，特别是在1935年第五次全国代表大会期间，该会要求男女平等，参与妇女参政运动。主席为王立明（Wong Lih-ming）小姐，系上海大学校长刘鸿恩博士（Dr. Herman C.E. Liu，音译）的夫人。

1.

Hand grenade thrown in the vicinity
of Sun Avenue, Bubbling Well Road.

At 9.50p.m. 15/2/38, C.P.W. 2118 on duty at Sun
Avenue (lane 1129), Bubbling Well Road, brought to the
station several pieces of a hand grenade of the "Potato
Masher" type and reported that a bomb was thrown at about
8.15p.m., even date, in the vicinity of House No.83, Sun
Avenue.

D.I. Toon, D.S. Deaville, C.D.C's 233 and 252 attended.
A survey of the scene revealed the following.
The hand grenade exploded on the flat roof of a block
of newly built garages situated approximately 20 yards
East of Sun Avenue and 150 yards South of Bubbling Well
Road.

A broken window pane in House No.83, Sun Avenue, was
the only damage done. The house has a first floor room
door which opens onto the garage roof.
The house is occupied by three families, they were
questioned and all stated that they had no political
connections and had not received any threatening letters.
They gave no intimation as to the reason for the bomb
throwing.

If the bomb thrower had wanted to injure any of the
house inmates, it would have been a simple matter for him
to have thrown the bomb through the window.

静安寺路孙家弄附近投掷手榴弹案。

1938年2月15日晚9时50分，在静安寺路孙家弄（1129弄）执勤的华捕2118号将数枚“马铃薯捣碎器”式手榴弹的碎片带至警局，并报告称，同日晚上约8时15分，在孙家弄83号房屋附近有人投掷了一枚炸弹。

巡官Toon、警佐Deaville、华探233号和252号到场。经现场勘查，情况如下。
手榴弹在一排新建车库的平顶上爆炸，该车库位于孙家弄以东约20码、静安寺路以南约150码处。

唯一的损害是孙家弄83号的一扇破碎窗玻璃。该房屋有一间一楼房间的门通向车库屋顶。
该房屋由三户家庭居住，经讯问，他们均表示与政治无关，也未收到任何恐吓信。
他们未提供关于投掷炸弹原因的任何线索。

如果投弹者意图伤害屋内的任何住户，他本可以轻易地将炸弹从窗户扔进去。

1/sheet 2.

A search of the ground was made with a view to
finding the hand grenade cap, but without result.
The U.S. Marine Camp at No.1051 Bubbling Well Road,
is situated approximately 100 yards to the North East of
the scene. A lane which runs along the East side of the
Camp compound, leads to the scene. The sentries knew
nothing of the explosion nor saw anyone enter or leave
the lane.
Between the Camp and the scene are a number of newly
built houses the majority of which are occupied by refugees.
To outward appearances the case has no political
significance.
The pieces of the hand grenade found at the scene
are being kept in the station.

为寻找手榴弹引信盖，对地面进行了搜索，但无结果。
静安寺路1051号的美国海军陆战队营地，位于事发地点东北方向约100码处。一条沿营地东侧延伸的小巷通向事发地点。哨兵对爆炸一事毫不知情，也未看见任何人进入或离开该小巷。
在营地与事发地点之间有一些新建房屋，其中大部分由难民居住。
从表面看，此案没有政治意义。
在现场发现的手榴弹碎片正保存在警局内。
